scenes.heading: Mutable vs Immutable Areas
scenes.narration: Maven. Mutable vs Immutable Areas. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: In AEM as a Cloud Service, which repository areas are immutable after startup?
scenes.heading: /apps and /libs
scenes.body: Section 2 says AEM as a Cloud Service requires strict separation of code and content, and specifically marks /apps and /libs as immutable.
scenes.narration: In AEM as a Cloud Service, which repository areas are immutable after startup? /apps and /libs. Section 2 says AEM as a Cloud Service requires strict separation of code and content, and specifically marks /apps and /libs as immutable.

scenes.question: What happens if code tries to create, update, or delete something in /apps at runtime after AEM starts?
scenes.heading: The attempt fails
scenes.body: The speech states that after AEM starts, you cannot create, update, or delete anything in /apps or /libs at runtime, and any attempt fails.

scenes.question: Which of these paths is listed as mutable in the speech?
scenes.heading: /conf
scenes.narration: Which of these paths is listed as mutable in the speech? /conf. The mutable list includes /content, /conf, /var, /etc, /system, /tmp, /home, and /oak:index.

scenes.question: Why can't a single content package deploy to both /apps and a mutable area in AEM as a Cloud Service?
scenes.heading: Because the application must split code and content into discrete packages
scenes.body: The speech says that due to the separation of immutable code and mutable content, a single package cannot deploy to both /apps and a mutable area, so the application must split them into discrete packages.

scenes.question: Which statement about /libs is correct?
scenes.heading: /libs must never be modified because only AEM product code is deployed there
scenes.body: The lesson says that, as in earlier versions, /libs must never be modified and only AEM product code is deployed there.

scenes.question: Given a scenario with Oak indexes in Cloud Service, how are index definitions treated for deployment?
scenes.heading: They are deployed as code in ui.apps
scenes.body: The speech calls Oak indexes a special case: although /oak:index is mutable at runtime, Cloud Manager waits for reindexing before switching code, so index definitions are deployed as code in ui.apps.

scenes.question: Why are Oak index definitions not treated like ordinary mutable content?
scenes.heading: Because Cloud Manager waits for the new index to be deployed and fully reindexed before switching to the new code image
scenes.body: The reason given is that Cloud Manager waits until a new index is deployed and fully reindexed before switching to the new code image.
